newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh opposition against buying India power.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh opposition against buying India power.

text.p: The main opposition party in the Bangladeshi parliament on Tuesday criticised a government plan to buy power from India, and said it amounted to giving away the keys to the country.

"The move is totally against the interest of the country and threatens to disrupt the country's industries," said Sheikh Razzak Ali, a member of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and former speaker of parliament.
As BNP legislators thumped desks and shouted slogans, Ali said the government was planning to "hand over the country's key to another country".

A serious electricity shortage in Bangladesh has prompted the Awami League government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to consider importing power from neighbouring India, Energy Minister Nooruddin Khan said earlier.
Bangladesh's current electricity requirements are 2,200 MW but the country faces a peak hour shortfall of 350 MW, the minister said.

Khan said India's eastern state of West Bengal, which borders Bangladesh, was unable to make up his country's entire peak hour shortfall, but that the Indian government had agreed to supply 300 MW of power from its national grid.
The requirements are expected to rise to 3,150 MW by the year 2000 and to 4,600 MW by 2005, energy officials said.
"Availability of power during peak hours, tariff and technical acceptability and getting the supply within the shortest possible time are the preconditions to be considered," Khan said.
The move to import electricity from India had been initiated by the BNP government of former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, Khan said in reply to Ali.
"The present government is just following up that move," Khan said, adding that Dhaka was also trying to boost local electricity generation by setting up new plants and repairing old ones.
Khan said the government was making efforts to boost generation capacity by up to 300 MW by renovating existing power plants by June this year.
